output.title: Spot free-tier limits before they interrupt your workflow
output.body:
If you run a small business, one practical workflow decision is simple: do you know when a free-tier tool is about to stop being free? That could be a SaaS plan, an API, an email tool, or any service that quietly turns a convenience into a bill or a block.

The useful question is not “Can this tool do the job?” It is “Do I know the quota, and do I check usage before the limit is hit?” If the answer is no, you are leaving the timing to the vendor. That is not a great control surface.

A plain next step is to pick one tool in your stack and write down three things: the free limit, where usage is visible, and what reminder will make you look at it. For some tools, a weekly calendar check is enough. For others, a vendor cost-alert email is better if usage moves fast. Boring works here.

Why it matters: if a free tier runs out unexpectedly, a workflow can pause or you may end up deciding on an upgrade under pressure. Early spotting does not remove the decision, but it keeps it human and deliberate.

Start with one tool, one quota, one reminder. Then move to the next.
